subject: pathology
title: Apoptotic Morphology, Annexin V, Necroptosis, and Pyroptosis

steps.tx: Under light microscopy, apoptotic cells appear as small, rounded or oval shrunken cells with intensely eosinophilic cytoplasm and dense pyknotic chromatin fragments. Also known in the liver as **Councilman bodies**, these apoptotic hepatocyte silhouettes are extruded into sinusoids during acute viral and autoimmune hepatitis without inciting adjacent necrosis.
steps.say: Councilman bodies are apoptotic hepatocytes with condensed eosinophilic cytoplasm seen in acute hepatitis.

vis.caption: Autoimmune liver inflammation demonstrating eosinophilic rounded Councilman bodies undergoing sinusoidal extrusion.
vis.alt: Histological view of apoptotic Councilman bodies in inflamed liver parenchyma

steps.tx: During early apoptosis before plasma membrane permeability is compromised, the normal asymmetrical lipid distribution of the bilayer collapses. Phosphatidylserine flips from the inner leaflet to the outer surface, where it can be detected in flow cytometry using calcium-dependent binding of fluorescently labeled **annexin V**.
steps.say: Annexin V binds externalized phosphatidylserine, identifying apoptotic cells by flow cytometry.

nodes.label: Healthy Cells Maintain Phosphatidylserine Exclusively in Inner Membrane Leaflet
Scramblase Flips Phosphatidylserine to External Surface of the Outer Leaflet
Fluorochrome-Conjugated Annexin V Binds Externalized PS in Calcium-Dependent Assay

steps.tx: In flow cytometric analysis, combining annexin V with a membrane-impermeant DNA-binding fluorophore distinguishes early apoptotic cells from late necrotic cells. While early apoptotic cells stain positive for annexin V but negative for propidium iodide, membrane-compromised necrotic cells stain positive for **both annexin V and propidium iodide**.
steps.say: Dual staining separates early apoptotic cells from late necrotic cells that admit propidium iodide.

left.title: Early Apoptosis (Annexin V+ / PI-)
points: Phosphatidylserine externalized to outer membrane leaflet
Plasma membrane remains structurally intact, excluding vital dyes
Propidium iodide cannot enter cytoplasm to stain nuclear DNA
Cells represent intact apoptotic bodies ready for phagocytic uptake

right.title: Necrosis / Late Apoptosis (Annexin V+ / PI+)
points: Phosphatidylserine exposed on external and internal membrane leaflets
Plasma membrane physically ruptured and completely permeable
Propidium iodide rapidly enters and intercalates into nuclear DNA
Reflects primary necrosis or un-engulfed secondary necrotic lysis

steps.tx: Not every membrane ruptured cell dies by accident. **Necroptosis** is programmed necrosis, run by RIPK and MLKL proteins when caspases are blocked, ending with MLKL punching holes in the membrane. The cell swells and bursts like ordinary necrosis, spilling contents that inflame surrounding tissue, yet the pathway is genetic and druggable. Viruses that inhibit caspases can push infected cells into this route, which helps explain its persistence in evolution.
steps.say: Necroptosis is programmed necrosis through RIPK and MLKL when caspases are blocked. The membrane ruptures and inflames tissue, but the pathway remains genetic and druggable.

vis.alt: Diagram of necroptosis, RIPK and MLKL proteins perforating the cell membrane of a swelling cell.
vis.caption: MLKL pores perforate the membrane of a swelling cell in necroptosis driven by RIPK signalling. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: When death receptors are stimulated under conditions where caspase-eight is pharmacologically or virally inhibited, cells activate an alternative regulated death pathway resembling necrosis. Known as **necroptosis**, this hybrid program features programmed molecular signaling that culminates in membrane rupture and inflammation.
steps.say: Necroptosis is programmed necrosis triggered when caspase-8 is blocked, causing inflammatory cell lysis.

vis.alt: Necroptosis signalling through RIPK1, RIPK3 and MLKL membrane pores when caspase-8 is blocked
vis.caption: Necroptosis signalling through RIPK1, RIPK3 and MLKL membrane pores when caspase-8 is blocked. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Execution of programmed necroptosis requires the assembly of a multi-protein signaling complex termed the necrosome. Receptor-interacting serine-threonine protein kinases RIPK1 and RIPK3 undergo reciprocal cross-phosphorylation, forming a fibrous amyloid-like core that recruits and directly phosphorylates the downstream executioner pseudo-kinase **mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein**.
steps.say: The necrosome forms as RIPK1 and RIPK3 cross-phosphorylate to activate the pore-forming protein MLKL.

nodes.label: TNF Binds TNFR1 While Caspase-8 Remains Blocked by Viral Inhibitors
RIPK1 and RIPK3 Dimerize and Autophosphorylate to Form the Necrosome
RIPK3 Phosphorylates Mixed Lineage Kinase Domain-Like Protein (MLKL)
Phosphorylated MLKL Oligomerizes, Inserting Directly into Plasma Membrane Pores

steps.tx: Phosphorylated mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein undergoes a conformational change that drives its oligomerization and translocation to the plasma membrane. By binding membrane phosphatidylinositol phosphates, MLKL pores disrupt membrane integrity, driving osmotic cell swelling and release of **damage-associated molecular patterns** that trigger inflammation.
steps.say: MLKL pores punch holes in the plasma membrane, driving osmotic lysis and releasing inflammatory DAMPs.

left.title: Apoptosis Features
points: Intact plasma membrane preserving intracellular contents
Forms non-inflammatory apoptotic bodies engulfed by macrophages
No release of cellular DAMPs; immunosuppressive microenvironment

right.title: Necroptosis Features
points: Pore formation by MLKL oligomers causes osmotic membrane lysis
Massive release of intracellular DAMPs (HMGB1, ATP, IL-1-alpha)
Triggers robust innate immune inflammation and leukocyte recruitment

steps.tx: A specialized form of programmed cell death intricately linked to the innate immune response is pyroptosis. Triggered by intracellular microbial pathogens such as Salmonella and Shigella, assembly of the cytosolic **inflammasome complex** activates caspase-one and caspase-four, driving intense inflammatory cytokine processing.
steps.say: Pyroptosis is an inflammasome-driven cell death pathway that activates caspase-1 to fight infections.

nodes.label: Intracellular Flagellin or Bacterial Toxins Recognized by NOD-Like Receptors
NLRP3 Associates with ASC Adapter to Assemble Multimeric Inflammasome
Procaspase-1 Cleaved into Active Caspase-1 (IL-1 Converting Enzyme)
Caspase-1 Cleaves Pro-IL-1-Beta and Pro-IL-18 into Active Secreted Cytokines

steps.tx: Active caspase-one cleaves the cytosolic pore-forming protein gasdermin D into an amino-terminal pore-forming domain. Oligomers of the **gasdermin D amino-terminal domain** insert into the plasma membrane to form large trans-membrane channels, causing cell swelling, lysis, and simultaneous release of interleukin-one beta and interleukin-eighteen.
steps.say: Cleaved gasdermin D forms large membrane pores that cause cell swelling and release of interleukin-1.

nodes.label: Active Caspase-1 Specifically Cleaves Autoinhibited Gasdermin D
Liberated N-Terminal Domain Binds Inner Membrane Phospholipids
Oligomerizes into 10-15 nm Pores, Breaking Ionic Equilibrium
Mature IL-1-Beta and IL-18 Flood out, Igniting Intense Pyrogenic Fever
